stem: A client receiving external-beam radiation therapy asks how to care for the skin in the treatment area. Which statement by the client indicates correct understanding?

options.A: I will use only skin products recommended by my radiation team and avoid heating pads or ice packs on the treatment area.
options.B: I will place an ice pack directly on the treatment area whenever the skin feels warm or irritated.
options.C: I can use any fragranced lotion or alcohol-based product as long as the skin has not started to peel.
options.D: I should scrub the treatment area firmly each day to remove dry or flaking skin before my radiation session.

rationale: NCI guidance advises clients receiving radiation therapy to use only skin products recommended by the healthcare team and to use gentle skin care because the treated skin may become dry, tender, irritated, or peel. NCI specifically advises not to use heating pads or ice packs on the radiation treatment area. Products containing alcohol or fragrance may irritate or dry the skin, and vigorous scrubbing can further injure sensitive tissue.
educational_objective: Teach gentle, team-directed skin care during radiation therapy and avoidance of direct heating pads or ice packs on the treatment field.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Skin and Nail Changes during Cancer Treatment; Radiation Therapy Side Effects
source_version_date: Skin and Nail Changes reviewed 2022-12-29; Radiation Therapy Side Effects reviewed 2025-05-15
source_locator: Skin and Nail Changes during Cancer Treatment — Ways to prevent or manage mild skin and nail changes: Use only recommended skin products; Protect your skin; Prevent or treat dry, itchy skin; Radiation Therapy Side Effects — skin changes by treatment area
source_claim_supported: NCI recommends team-directed gentle skin care during radiation therapy, use of recommended products, avoidance of heating pads and ice packs on the treatment area, and avoidance of irritating products such as those containing alcohol or fragrance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — personal hygiene, comfort measures, and nonpharmacological supportive nursing care
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — radiation-treatment skin care and comfort
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original radiation-skin-care item around specific NCI-supported self-care actions. Removed vague 'harsh products/extreme temperatures' wording and generic ONS sourcing, replaced them with exact NCI guidance on recommended skin products and avoidance of heating pads/ice packs, and remapped the item from Safety and Infection Prevention and Control to Basic Care and Comfort because the tested construct is supportive skin care rather than infection transmission.
audit_findings: Original item used broad, partly protocol-dependent wording and was misclassified under infection prevention.
NCI directly supports using only recommended skin products and avoiding heating pads or ice packs on the radiation treatment area.
The final item avoids prescribing a specific lotion, wash frequency, or product not supported for every radiation field and regimen.
Blueprint mapping was corrected to Basic Care and Comfort because the question tests supportive skin care and comfort measures.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct response with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, or unresolved source conflict.
